content: Why does docs#SuperChain exist? It's only used in three other predicates (https://loogle.lean-lang.org/?q=SuperChain) and it seems to me like it could reasonably be written down as just two separate predicates.
I agree, it's just ancient and could use a refactor
They seem to exist from the beginning: https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib3/commit/deb168147d4ede8848940a797753f026648501a4

Wow, I guess Zorn is just really really really fundamental
FWIW the stuff in file#Order/CompleteLattice/Chain also seem rather odd to me, but I haven't thought about whether a proof of Zorn can avoid them
Oh, they exist because they are ported from Isabelle. https://dist.isabelle.cit.tum.de/dist/library/HOL/HOL/Zorn.html
Oh, which is itself ported from Isabelle/ZF (1994), which is based on an unpublished article

Snir Broshi said:

Wow, I guess Zorn is just really really really fundamental
FWIW the stuff in file#Order/CompleteLattice/Chain also seem rather odd to me, but I haven't thought about whether a proof of Zorn can avoid them

(warning, self promotion ahead) you can avoid, sort of, but not quite. Here is a proof that avoids Hausdorff Maximality Principle, but I like HMP very much (even far more than ZL).

N.B.: We defined our own version of "SuperChain", but with being an initial segment.

Pedro Sánchez Terraf said:

the simplest proof of Zorn's Lemma

Nice, but it's more than twice as long and defines even more proprietary definitions.

Also I'm not sure why avoiding Hausdorff is the goal, it's great; I meant avoid proprietary definitions.

Actually "the simplest" applies to the original informal (Incatasciato's) proof that appears in Appendix A of the paper; and why we claim that, is argued on the main text.
The goal was not to have an optimal presentation for a library.
